title: Proper-support normalization identifies the full etale right-adjoint exchange mate
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $e:U\to X$ a separated etale finite-type morphism and $w:X'\to X$ any morphism of Noetherian schemes (finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings) [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Form $U'=U\times_XX'$ with projections $e':U'\to X'$ and $w':U'\to U$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Choose a compactification $c=(j,r)$ of $e$ and first use its pullback $c'=(j',r')$ for $e'$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. In the ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], put $F_e=Rr_*Dj_!$, $F_{e'}=Rr'_*Dj'_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and fix any adjunctions $F_e\dashv G_e$, $F_{e'}\dashv G_{e'}$ with counits $\varepsilon_e,\varepsilon_{e'}$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Put $S_a=D(a_{\Sigma!})\dashv a^*$ with counit $\operatorname{ev}_a$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. Use the proper-support/sum comparison $d_a:F_a\xrightarrow{\sim}S_a$ of [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact], and its conjugate $\rho_a=(d_a^{-1})^c:G_a\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate].

Let $C=C_{e,w}:w^*F_e\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{e'}w'^*$ be the specified proper exchange followed by inverse open-extension exchange [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], and let $b^\Sigma:w^*S_e\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{e'}w'^*$ be the degreewise inverse of the specified sum comparison [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map] [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules]. Their inverse comparison is
$$C^{-1}\circ(d_{e'}^{-1}w'^*)=w^*(d_e^{-1})\circ(b^\Sigma)^{-1}.$$
For every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ let $B_{e,w,K}:w'^*G_eK\to G_{e'}w^*K$ be the $F_{e'}\dashv G_{e'}$ adjunct of $w^*\varepsilon_{e,K}\circ C^{-1}_{G_eK}$. Then
$$\rho_{e',w^*K}\circ B_{e,w,K}=\chi_K\circ w'^*\rho_{e,K},$$
where $\chi_K:w'^*e^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}e'^*w^*K$ is the canonical inverse-image composition map [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Equivalently, the common $S_{e'}\dashv e'^*$ transpose of these two morphisms is
$$w^*\varepsilon_{e,K}\circ C^{-1}_{G_eK}\circ d_{e'}^{-1}(w'^*G_eK)=\operatorname{ev}_{e',w^*K}\circ S_{e'}(\chi_K\circ w'^*\rho_{e,K}).$$
These are identities of natural transformations on the whole unbounded categories. They agree with the canonical proper-refinement identifications for $c$ and $c'$, hence also with any other chosen compactifications. No finiteness of the proper compactification map $r$ and no etaleness or flatness of $w$ is assumed.
For $a=e,e'$ this conjugate is uniquely characterized by the counit identity
$$\operatorname{ev}_{a,K}\circ S_a(\rho_{a,K})=\varepsilon_{a,K}\circ d_a^{-1}(G_aK).$$

proof.text: For $a=e,e'$, specialize the transpose characterization in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] to $L_1=F_a$, $R_1=G_a$, $L_2=S_a$, $R_2=a^*$, $G=H=\mathrm{id}$ and $\alpha=d_a^{-1}$. It says exactly $\operatorname{ev}_{a,K}S_a(\rho_{a,K})=\varepsilon_{a,K}d_a^{-1}(G_aK)$. The transpose bijection makes this characterization unique. proof.text:
Fix arbitrary $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and put $M=G_eK$. Write $T=w^*\varepsilon_{e,K}C_M^{-1}d_{e'}^{-1}(w'^*M)$. Step 1, Step 2, naturality of $(b^\Sigma)^{-1}$ at $\rho_{e,K}:M\to e^*K$, and the derived counit equation of [lem-pur-etale-sum-exchange-counit], respectively, give
$$\begin{aligned}T&=w^*(\varepsilon_{e,K}d_e^{-1}(M))(b^\Sigma_M)^{-1}\\&=w^*\operatorname{ev}_{e,K}\,w^*S_e(\rho_{e,K})(b^\Sigma_M)^{-1}\\&=w^*\operatorname{ev}_{e,K}(b^\Sigma_{e^*K})^{-1}S_{e'}(w'^*\rho_{e,K})\\&=\operatorname{ev}_{e',w^*K}S_{e'}(\chi_K\circ w'^*\rho_{e,K}).\end{aligned}$$
This is the displayed common-transpose identity. The cited equation is already on the whole unbounded derived category, so no detection by cohomology or boundedness argument is used.

proof.text: The $S_{e'}\dashv e'^*$ transpose of $\rho_{e',w^*K}B_{e,w,K}$ is $\operatorname{ev}_{e',w^*K}S_{e'}(\rho_{e',w^*K})S_{e'}(B_{e,w,K})$. By Step 2 and naturality of $d_{e'}^{-1}$ this equals $\varepsilon_{e',w^*K}F_{e'}(B_{e,w,K})d_{e'}^{-1}(w'^*G_eK)=T$, by the defining transpose of $B$. Step 3 identifies $T$ with the transpose of $\chi_K\circ w'^*\rho_{e,K}$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] proves the required equality. All maps are natural in $K$, hence it is an equality of natural transformations.

First identify every normalized support comparison in etaleSupportMapCompatibility with the fixed graph comparison. The inclusion of open extension into direct image is monic: use the sectionwise injectivity of openExtensionProperSupport_range, preservation of monomorphisms by direct image, and the direct-image composition isomorphism. Cancel this inclusion in the two sheaf normalization equations, then use full faithfulness of precomposition with the homotopy localization and the derived normalization equations to identify the derived comparisons. Apply the refinement clause of etaleSupportMapCompatibility to Compactification.inf c d and its two projections, then the common-refinement cocycle from unboundedEtaleCompactSupport_comparison_coherence to get t ≫ d_d.hom = d_c.hom. Invert this equation and apply conjugateEquiv_comp to prove rightAdjointIso_refinement. Transport inverse_comparison to arbitrary target compactifications using the same comparison identity. This identifies the two sides of the exchange refinement square after precomposition with the invertible target support comparison. Finally transpose the square under the chosen target adjunction: naturality of the source conjugate, conjugateEquiv_counit and mateEquiv_counit show that the two transposes agree. Injectivity of the adjunction hom equivalence proves rightMate_refinement for arbitrary compactifications.
